partner_context.their_ambition: Uber is the world's mobility demand layer — one app for rides, and increasingly the front-end for autonomous fleets it doesn't have to own. The strategy is platform-over-assets: aggregate demand, partner for supply, and add every viable mode.
partner_context.their_pressure: Land ride-hail is mature in Uber's core markets. The growth edges are new surfaces (air, water), autonomy, and premium tiers — and rivals are moving on all three.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the water-mobility supply layer for Uber's demand engine: a software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that plugs into the Uber app exactly like Uber's robotaxi partners do — mode by mode, city by city.

hero.title: Uber × Navier — the water layer of the world's mobility platform
hero.subtitle: Uber aggregates demand and partners for supply. Navier is the foiling water supply — autonomy-ready, app-native.
hero.what_we_do_together: Uber adds a foiling water tier the same way it adds robotaxis: Navier supplies the software-defined fleet and runs the network; Uber supplies the demand, the app, and the rider relationship. We start where Uber is already pushing the frontier — the autonomous-forward Gulf — then extend to coastal metros worldwide.

why_now: Uber and WeRide are deploying 1,200 robotaxis across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Riyadh by 2027, in partnership with Dubai's RTA. Uber has shown it will put partner-operated autonomous fleets in its app. Navier's software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling vessels are the same model on the water — and a ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026).
multimodal_fit: Same playbook as Uber's robotaxi partnerships: partner-operated supply, Uber-owned demand and rider experience. The water leg books door-to-door with an UberX at each pier — one app, one account, a new surface.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: On-demand foiling transfers in-app — the at-scale proof case.

differentiation.vs_ferry: Scheduled public ferries are a different product. Navier in the Uber app is on-demand, premium, door-to-door — a ride, not a timetable.
differentiation.vs_candela: Foiling competitors validate the category. Navier's edge for Uber is the software-defined, autonomy-ready architecture that mirrors Uber's robotaxi model, plus a hybrid long-range option with no charging-infrastructure dependency.
differentiation.navier_moat: Software-defined and autonomy-ready, a Turkey factory for supply, a marquee cap table, and at-scale proof in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: Uber already runs partner-operated autonomous fleets.
proof_points.evidence: Uber + WeRide: 1,200 robotaxis across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Riyadh by 2027, with Dubai RTA.

proof_points.claim: The water network is real and at scale.

objections.concern: Why water for a ride-hail platform?
objections.response: Because Uber's coastal markets — the Gulf, NYC, Miami, the Bay, SE Asia — lose hours to congestion on trips that are minutes by water. It's incremental demand on a surface no competitor has claimed.

objections.concern: Does Uber have to operate boats?
objections.response: No — same as robotaxis. Navier (or a local operator) runs the fleet; Uber supplies demand and the app.

markets.label: US

hero.title: Uber × Navier — beating coastal gridlock in the Uber app

hero.what_we_do_together: A premium foiling water tier in the Uber app across the US's most congested waterfront metros — the on-demand answer to bridge-and-tunnel gridlock. Navier supplies the fleet; Uber supplies the demand.

markets.why_now: Uber owns US ride-hail demand and is expanding premium and autonomous tiers. Navier's US unit economics benchmark a foiling trip against helicopter and seaplane shuttles at a fraction of the experience friction — a natural Uber premium product. (Economics in the deck.)
